Title: Valid login opens mailbox
Steps: Open login; enter email+password; submit
Expected Result: Mailbox loads; compose button visible; URL on mail.proton.me
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Gate to every journey; stable, deterministic and cheap, so it runs on every PR.

Title: Wrong password rejected
Steps: Open login; enter valid email + wrong password; submit
Expected Result: Error shown; no mailbox; login form remains
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Security-relevant negative path; the error and the 'no mailbox' state are easy to assert reliably.

Title: Logout then Back does not restore session
Steps: Log out; press browser Back
Expected Result: Login form shown; mailbox not accessible
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Session-security regression (Back after logout) that is easy to miss manually each release; repeatable.

Title: Empty username/password validation
Steps: Submit empty form
Expected Result: Field validation shown
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Already covered indirectly by AUTH-02; client-side validation adds little extra regression value.

Title: CAPTCHA / lockout after repeated failures
Steps: Fail login repeatedly
Expected Result: Verification or throttling appears
Rationale (why automate / why manual): CAPTCHA/lockout is built to block bots and is intermittent; needs a human to observe.

Title: Send mail sender->receiver (E2E) and record delivery latency
Steps: Compose to receiver with subject/body; send; open receiver inbox; open message
Expected Result: Receiver sees subject+body; Sent contains message
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Core P0 journey across two accounts; a break blocks users; deterministic with unique data.

Title: Invalid recipient blocks send
Steps: Compose; recipient 'not-an-email-address'; send
Expected Result: Recipient error; composer stays open; nothing in Sent
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Validation negative case; fast, stable, and proves bad input never sends.

Title: To + CC recipients handled
Steps: Compose to receiver cc sender; send
Expected Result: Sent has message; receiver inbox and CC copy in sender inbox
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Useful but overlaps the COMP-01 flow and is lower risk; documented, trimmed from the suite.
Notes: lower risk; trimmed to keep suite focused

Title: BCC recipient hidden from others
Steps: Send with BCC; inspect headers
Expected Result: BCC address not visible to To recipients
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Header-level check needs a third mailbox; the two-account variant is automated as COMP-11.

Title: Empty subject send confirmation
Steps: Send with empty subject
Expected Result: Confirmation dialog appears
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Dialog wording/behaviour needs observation and is low risk; explore manually.

Title: Auto-save persists after reload
Steps: Compose; fill fields; wait for saved; close; reload; reopen
Expected Result: Draft in Drafts; content intact after reload
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Auto-save and reload persistence is a core promise; waits on the saved indicator, no sleeps.

Title: Draft -> sent transition
Steps: Create draft; open from Drafts; send
Expected Result: Removed from Drafts; present in Sent
Rationale (why automate / why manual): State transition (Drafts -> Sent) with assertions on both folders.

Title: Discard draft
Steps: Create draft; discard
Expected Result: Draft removed
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Overlaps DRAFT-06; explored manually.

Title: Mark read/unread
Steps: Select; mark read; mark unread
Expected Result: Unread class toggles correctly
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Core message state; stable assertion on the unread marker; P1.

Title: Star message
Steps: Star message; open Starred
Expected Result: Message in Starred and still in Inbox
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Lower risk and similar mechanics to other actions; trimmed from the suite.
Notes: lower risk; trimmed to keep suite focused

Title: Trash and restore
Steps: Trash; open Trash; move to Inbox
Expected Result: Moves Inbox -> Trash -> Inbox
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Multi-step state transition (Inbox -> Trash -> Inbox) with high regression value.

Title: Bulk actions on multiple messages
Steps: Select several; archive
Expected Result: All move together
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Same code path as single actions; extra setup cost for little new coverage.
Notes: extra setup; same code path as single-item

Title: Move message to a custom folder
Preconditions: Receiver session; fixture folder QA-Folder (created once)
Steps: Seed mail; select it; Move to QA-Folder; open the folder
Expected Result: Message leaves Inbox and is listed in QA-Folder
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Required scope area (folders); organisation is a core mail feature; a reusable fixture folder avoids free-plan limits.

Title: Keyword search
Steps: Search unique keyword
Expected Result: Only matching message listed
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Core search behaviour with a positive and negative assertion; P1.

Title: Advanced keyword+sender+folder
Steps: Advanced search with all three; then wrong sender
Expected Result: Match found; wrong sender returns no results
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Required multi-condition case; checks AND semantics by changing one condition.

Title: No-result and reset
Steps: Search nonsense; clear
Expected Result: No-result state; reset restores list
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Empty state and reset are low risk; trimmed from the suite.
Notes: lower risk; trimmed to keep suite focused

Title: Subject filter archives matching mail only
Steps: Create filter; send matching + non-matching; verify; delete filter
Expected Result: Matching to Archive; non-matching in Inbox; filter removed
Rationale (why automate / why manual): End-to-end rule behaviour (match vs non-match) with guaranteed clean-up; required area.

Title: Disable/edit filter
Steps: Toggle off; send matching
Expected Result: Mail stays in Inbox
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Toggle/edit UI changes often and needs observation first.

Title: Undo send then resend
Steps: Send; click Undo in toast; verify composer + Sent; resend; wait toast gone; check Sent + receiver
Expected Result: No message after undo; exactly one after resend
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Timing/state-dependent flow; demonstrates state-based waiting instead of sleeps.

Title: Scheduled send create/cancel
Steps: Schedule for future; verify Scheduled folder; cancel
Expected Result: Appears under Scheduled; cancel removes it
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Needs real elapsed time; discuss clock-control or mocking rather than long tests.

Title: Attachment round trip
Steps: Attach file; send; receiver opens; download
Expected Result: Filename preserved; downloaded content identical
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Proves file integrity end to end (name + downloaded content) across two accounts; P1 and deterministic.

Title: Large/oversized attachment
Steps: Attach file above size limit
Expected Result: Clear error
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Oversized uploads are slow and limits must be confirmed from the docs first.

Title: Password-protected email
Steps: Send with password; open as external
Expected Result: Requires password to read
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Needs an external recipient and password sharing; cannot be done safely in CI.

Title: Send to external @gmail.com address accepted
Preconditions: Sender session; a Gmail test mailbox
Steps: Compose to a gmail address; send; check Sent; check Gmail inbox
Expected Result: UI accepts address; Sent shows message; no bounce; arrives in Gmail (not E2E encrypted)
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Needs an external Gmail mailbox we do not control; third-party delivery cannot be verified reliably in CI.
Notes: needs a Gmail mailbox; automate only the UI-accept part

Title: Malformed recipient variants rejected
Steps: Try each value as recipient and click Send
Test Data: missing@ ; @domain.com ; plain text ; a b@x.com ; a@@x.com ; a@x..com ; a@x ; emoji@x.com
Expected Result: Error shown for each; composer stays open; nothing in Sent
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Same check over many malformed inputs; parameterization makes it cheap and it protects a P0 validation rule.

Title: Valid format but non-existent Proton address
Steps: Send to nobody-<random>@proton.me
Expected Result: UI accepts send; a delivery-failure notice arrives in sender inbox (verify real behaviour)
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Bounce timing and format are decided by mail servers and are unpredictable; observe manually.

Title: Duplicate recipient in To
Steps: Add same address twice
Expected Result: Chip de-duplicated or single copy delivered
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Expected behaviour is not defined; explore first, then decide whether to automate.

Title: Send with no recipient
Steps: Fill subject/body only; click Send
Expected Result: Blocked with clear error; no message sent
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Simple, deterministic P0 validation; good candidate for the next iteration.

Title: BCC privacy (two accounts)
Steps: To = sender (self); BCC = receiver; send; open message in BOTH mailboxes
Expected Result: Receiver gets mail; sender copy does not list the BCC address to other recipients
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Privacy-critical (BCC leak = high impact); two accounts make it verifiable and deterministic.

Title: Subject/body boundary and special content
Steps: Send with long subject (250+ chars); emoji; <script> text; empty body
Expected Result: Delivered intact; HTML-looking text shown as text (no injection); empty body allowed
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Boundary and special-character inputs expose rendering/injection bugs; small param set keeps cost low (next iteration).

Title: Many recipients and CC/BCC limits
Steps: Add many recipients
Expected Result: Limit enforced with clear message (verify documented limit)
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Limits are unknown and need exploration before any assertion can be written.

Title: Sent item has correct recipients subject body timestamp
Steps: Send; open Sent item
Expected Result: All fields match what was typed; timestamp within a minute of send
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Confirms the final state of the send flow; partly covered by COMP-01, full field check is next iteration.

Title: No leftover draft after send
Steps: Send; open Drafts
Expected Result: Draft removed; exactly one Sent copy
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Covered by the draft-to-sent transition in DRAFT-02; documented for completeness.

Title: Receiver gets exactly one copy
Steps: Send; wait; count matches by subject
Expected Result: Count = 1 (no duplicates)
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Duplicate-delivery check is valuable but moderate risk; next iteration.

Title: Deleting Sent copy does not delete receiver copy
Steps: Send; trash sent copy; check receiver inbox
Expected Result: Receiver copy unaffected
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Needs a destructive step across two mailboxes and is low risk; manual.

Title: Send-to-receive latency measured
Steps: Record time at Send; poll receiver inbox; record arrival; log seconds
Expected Result: Delivered within agreed threshold (suggest 30 s; log value in report)
Suite Status: Folded into COMP-01 (latency logged to reports/metrics.csv)
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Measured inside the existing E2E test so no extra test is needed; gives evidence of async delivery time.

Title: Allowed file types matrix
Steps: Send each type and download
Test Data: pdf ; png ; jpg ; docx ; zip ; txt
Expected Result: All sent and downloaded intact
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Type matrix is cheap to parameterize but the core round trip is already automated (ATTACH-01); next iteration.

Title: Blocked or risky types (exe/js/bat)
Steps: Attach executable-type file; send
Expected Result: Record actual behaviour (allowed/warned/blocked) and compare with docs
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Risky-type handling is policy-driven and may change; needs human judgement against the docs.

Title: Size boundaries
Steps: Attach below / near / above limit (verify limit in Proton docs: message size and attachment total)
Expected Result: Below and near send OK; above shows clear error and does not send
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Large uploads are slow and costly in CI; run manually or nightly.
Notes: large files slow; run nightly if automated

Title: Number of attachments (e.g. 10 images) and max count
Steps: Attach 10 small images; then try to exceed documented count
Expected Result: All 10 listed and delivered; over-limit blocked with message
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Ten-image case is easy to automate later; the true limit needs exploration.

Title: Remove attachment before send
Steps: Attach; remove; send
Expected Result: Receiver gets mail with NO attachment
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Real defect risk (removed file still sent); fast and deterministic with a clear assertion.

Title: Draft keeps attachment after reload
Steps: Attach; wait for saved; close; reload; reopen draft
Expected Result: Attachment still present with same name
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Draft persistence with attachments is explicitly required; checks server-side state, not just the UI.

Title: Odd filenames and zero-byte file
Steps: Attach file with spaces/unicode/long name; attach 0-byte file
Expected Result: Name preserved or clearly sanitised; zero-byte handled with message
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Odd filenames and zero-byte files are exploratory edge cases with low frequency.

Title: Unread counter updates (new / read / unread)
Steps: Note count; receive mail; open it; mark unread
Expected Result: Counter +1 on arrival; -1 after read; +1 after mark unread
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Counter logic is valuable, but needs stable counter locators first; next iteration.
Notes: new accounts start with 2 unread Proton welcome mails: assert deltas, never absolute counts

Title: Read/unread state persists after reload and new session
Steps: Mark read; reload; mark unread; reload; open in a new context
Expected Result: State identical after reload and in a fresh session (server-side)
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Server-side persistence of read/unread catches state-sync bugs; deterministic across reload and new session.

Title: Opening a message marks it read automatically
Steps: Open unread message; return to list
Expected Result: Row shown as read; counter decremented
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Auto-mark-read is a visible behaviour; next iteration once counters are stable.

Title: New-mail notification
Steps: Receive mail while app is open
Expected Result: Browser/desktop notification and tab-title count appear (verify behaviour)
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Depends on browser/OS permissions and is unreliable headless; manual.

Title: Bulk select and mark read/unread
Steps: Select all; mark read; mark unread
Expected Result: All rows change state together
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Same logic as single-item actions; exploratory spot check is enough.

Title: Auto-save with partial content
Steps: Save drafts with only subject / only body / only recipient
Expected Result: Each saved and reopens with same partial content
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Partial-content drafts are good param candidates; next iteration.

Title: Editing a draft updates it (no duplicate)
Steps: Create draft; reopen; change subject; wait saved; check Drafts
Expected Result: One draft with new subject; old subject absent
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Guards the duplicate-draft bug class; clear before/after assertion.

Title: Discard draft removes it
Steps: Create draft; click Discard; check Drafts (and Trash)
Expected Result: Draft gone from Drafts (record whether it goes to Trash)
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Valuable, but the expected Trash behaviour must be confirmed first; next iteration.

Title: Delete draft from Drafts folder then restore
Steps: Select draft; delete; restore from Trash
Expected Result: Moves Drafts -> Trash -> Drafts
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Lower risk; mirrors the inbox trash/restore test.

Title: Closing an empty composer creates no draft
Steps: Open composer; close without typing
Expected Result: No empty draft in Drafts
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Low risk edge case; next iteration.

Title: Draft visible from a second browser session
Steps: Create draft in context A; open mailbox in context B
Expected Result: Draft present in B (server-side persistence)
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Proves the draft is stored on the server, not only in the local browser; deterministic.

Title: Reload while composing before auto-save
Steps: Type; reload immediately
Expected Result: Record what is lost or kept (possible data-loss risk)
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Data-loss timing depends on races; needs human exploration.

Title: Offline/online during composing
Steps: Go offline; type; go online
Expected Result: Draft saved after reconnect; no silent loss
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Network conditions are hard to reproduce reliably; manual.

Title: Same draft open in two tabs
Steps: Edit in both tabs
Expected Result: No silent overwrite/duplicate (record behaviour)
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Concurrency behaviour is undefined and low priority; manual.

Title: Create label; apply and remove
Steps: Create label; apply to message; verify under label; remove label
Expected Result: Message appears under the label, then disappears after removal
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Free plans cap labels (3) and cleanup is UI-heavy; verify manually and record behaviour.

Title: Folder/label creation limit on free plan
Steps: Create folders/labels until the limit
Expected Result: Clear upgrade/limit message; no silent failure
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Plan limits are policy and change; observe, do not automate.

Title: Category tabs (Primary/Social/Promotions/Newsletters) routing
Steps: Send person-to-person mail; check which tab shows it
Expected Result: Mail from the other test account lands in Primary
Rationale (why automate / why manual): Automation risk: waitForMessage only sees the current tab; observe real routing first.
